title: Normalize operator-role-schema and augment audit context with KMS-origin validation
author: Maya Chen
release_notes:
- Introduce normalized operator role schema (v2) and a migration tool to convert legacy bindings.
- Add audit context enrichment with request provenance and KMS-origin metadata.
- Enforce KMS-region validation for tenant-scoped encryption operations behind a runtime gate.
- Backwards-compatible shadow mode for gradual rollout; no customer-facing breaking changes.
description:
Motivation: Operator role bindings and service-scoped RBAC had accumulated multiple informal cases (legacy labels, ad-hoc attributes) that complicate decision logic and lead to audit gaps when requests cross region boundaries. This PR provides three coordinated pieces: 1) a canonical operator-role schema (v2) with explicit fields for scope, residency_intent, and operator_class; 2) audit enrichment that attaches a compact provenance header (X-RW-Provenance) containing the service principal, request path, and KMS-origin fingerprint; 3) a lightweight KMS-region validator that asserts the CMK origin matches tenant residency expectations before allowing encrypt/decrypt calls. All changes are behind rollout controls and include a migration path.

What this PR does (high level):
- service/authz: add role_schema_v2.go and conversion helpers to read legacy bindings and synthesize the v2 canonical representation. Exposes NormalizeOperatorRole(binding) and ValidateOperatorScope(role).
- service/audit: add enrichment hook that attaches request provenance and KMS origin to the audit envelope. Adds an opt-in header extractor and structured audit fields (provenance.kms_origin, provenance.operator_class).
- service/kms: introduce region_validator.go that verifies a CMK descriptor has an allowed region claim and wires into the KMS client path; validation is configurable per-tenant via ResidencyPolicy.
- cmd/migrations: add role-schema-normalize tool that can run in shadow or apply mode; emits a dry-run report compatible with the Console migration UI.
- infra/helm: add a runtime flag rbac_v2.normalize_enabled and rbac_v2.enforce_kms_region with sensible defaults (false for strict enforcement).
- tests: unit tests for schema conversion, integration tests exercising cross-region KMS requests with enriched audit, and an e2e test that exercises the migration tool output.

Checklist: [x] Unit tests added and green. [x] Integration tests added (flaky first run rerun). [x] Migration tool with dry-run mode included. [x] Runtime flags and feature gates added. [x] Documentation page describing migration steps.

Migration notes: The cmd/migrations/role-schema-normalize binary reads the current binding store and produces a line-delimited JSON report (both normalized candidate and diff against legacy). Operators can run in dry-run to review changes and then run --apply to write normalized bindings into the binding-store. The tool preserves historical audit references via an injected legacy_id field. Migration is idempotent.

Operational impact and rollout: By default enforcement is disabled. We ship in three phases: 1) shadow-mode enrichment (collect provenance/kms_origin in audits) 2) normalization rollout (migrations + runtime gate to prefer v2 roles when present) 3) optional enforcement (rbac_v2.enforce_kms_region=true) once residency policy coverage reaches >95% in dry-run. The helm values include a TTL for shadow evidence to limit storage.

Security review summary: The KMS-region validator defers to tenant ResidencyPolicy; it explicitly rejects operations that would use a CMK with a mismatched region claim when enforcement is on. We added ACL checks to the migration tool to ensure only cluster-admins can apply changes. Audit enrichment avoids logging full CMK material — only a stable fingerprint (sha256) and region claim are included.

Backward compatibility: Legacy bindings continue to be evaluated by the authorization engine while NormalizeOperatorRole runs in the background; if both legacy and v2 bindings exist the decision path prefers the explicit v2 when the feature gate is enabled. No callers should see immediate change when enforcement is off.

Notes about verification: e2e tests use a small fake-KMS provider that exposes region_claim headers; CI runs include an integration profile that exercises the validator, and we added a circuit breaker to avoid increased latencies on KMS calls.
commits_summary: 1) initial role schema and conversion helpers; 2) audit enrichment hook + tests; 3) KMS region validator and wiring; 4) migration tool + CLI; 5) helm flags and docs; 6) integration/e2e tests and flake fixes.
